title: NCT 127 Open 10th-Anniversary ‘Neo City: The Redline’ Tour With Sold-Out Seoul Run
summary: The 'Neo City: The Redline' tour continues across Asia through January 2027.
body: NCT 127 have kicked off their fifth headlining tour, ‘ Neo City: The Redline ‘, with a sold-out three-night run in Seoul that doubled as a celebration of the group’s 10th anniversary. The K-pop act performed the final Seoul show of the run on Saturday (Sept. 20, local time) at KSPO Dome in Olympic Park, capping three days of concerts that began Sept. 18. The shows sold out completely — including restricted-view seats — drawing roughly 31,500 fans, according to the group’s label, SM Entertainment. Performing as a five-member lineup, the group leaned into ambitious staging throughout the set. The opening number, “Legacy,” saw the members descend through the air on wires, while “Punch” was staged against a boxing-ring-style arena setup with a large troupe of dancers. For “Piñata,” the members arrived onstage in a real vehicle, picking up from a pre-recorded video segment. Leader Taeyong also debuted a newly written rap verse for the fan-favorite “Cherry Bomb,” reflecting the group’s evolution over the past decade. The set built to an extended medley of hits including “Fire Truck,” “Fact Ch…

title: Ninajirachi Adds 12 North American Dates to ‘I Love My Computer’ Tour
summary: The award-winning Australian producer extends her North American run into 2027 amid surging demand
body: Ninajirachi is expanding her North American touring, adding 12 new dates to the I Love My Computer and It Loves Me tour that push the run into early 2027. The additional shows follow the Australian producer’s initial seven-date North American leg and reflect what promoters have described as surging demand. The new dates open Nov. 19 in San Francisco before a January run through Portland, Seattle, Minneapolis, Chicago, Cincinnati, Atlanta, Charlotte, Washington, D.C., New York, Toronto and Montreal. Rising producer IKEDA will open all the new shows. A presale begins Wednesday (Sept. 24), followed by the general on-sale Thursday (Sept. 25), both at 10 a.m. local time. The expansion caps a breakout stretch for the 26-year-old, born Nina Wilson. Her 2025 debut album I Love My Computer — a concept record about her relationship with computers and the internet — peaked at No. 12 on the ARIA Albums Chart and drew the most nominations of any artist at the 2025 ARIA Awards, winning three, including Best Solo Artist. The album also took the 2025 Australian Music Prize for Album of the Year and triple j’s Album of the Year, cementing her as one of the country’s fastest-risin…

title: Google expands Motion Assist beyond Pixel phones with latest Play Services update
summary: The update also includes improvements for metrics shared from Wear OS watches to phones, along with several other changes.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google is rolling out Motion Assist to more Android phones through the latest Google Play services update. The feature uses moving visual bubbles around the edges of your screen that match a vehicle’s movement to help reduce motion sickness. You need a phone running Android 17 or newer and an up-to-date version of Google Play services to use it. Google’s Motion Assist feature is now moving beyond Pixel devices to more Android phones thanks to the latest Google Play services update.

title: Google officially opens the door to more games on Android Auto
summary: Games on Android Auto and Android Automotive OS are officially out of beta.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google has officially moved games on Android Auto and Android Automotive OS out of beta and made them generally available. You can already play supported games on your car’s screen while parked by browsing through Google’s collection of games for Android Auto and Android Automotive, but developers can now publish compatible titles to Google Play’s open testing and production tracks. Android Auto and Android Automotive games are blocked while you’re driving for obvious safety reasons. If you’ve ever found yourself sitting in your car with nothing to do, Google is ramping up options for your entertainment. In addition to onboarding video streaming services on Android Auto and Android Automotive, Google is also making in-car gaming a bigger deal this year.

title: The smart glasses market has more than doubled in the last year, with Meta dominating
summary: Smart glasses had a huge first half of 2026, with Meta way out in front and display-less models accounting for 96%.
body: Credit: Chase Bernath / Android Authority TL;DR Global AI glasses shipments jumped 263% year over year in H1 2026, according to Counterpoint Research. Display-less models accounted for 96% of shipments, with Meta holding a dominant 94% share of that segment. Shipments of AR glasses surged 449% year over year, albeit from a low base. Smart glasses might still feel like a niche category of tech, but they seem to be selling at a much faster clip than they were a year ago. Global AI glasses shipments jumped 263% year over year in the first half of 2026, and the vast majority weren’t AR specs. Counterpoint Research’s latest Intelligent Eyewear Market Tracker attributes most of that growth to the cheaper, more mature display-less category, which includes products such as the Ray-Ban Meta AI Glasses. Shipments in this segment rose 258% year over year and 22% compared with the second half of 2025.

title: Google Sheets just got a little better for the financial analysts out there
summary: Google Sheets is getting a new add-on to help you build dynamic financial reports.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Workspace is giving Google Sheets a new add-on. Workday for Google Sheets eliminates the need for manual CSV downloads. This add-on will be available to all Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal accounts. Google Sheets users have been getting spoiled these last few weeks. Earlier this month, Gemini became available for the Sheets Android app. That update came only days after the tech giant expanded the number of available fonts . Now, Google is giving a gift to the financial analysts out there. Today, the Mountain View-based firm introduced a new add-on called Workday for Google Sheets. Available in the Google Workspace Marketplace, this add-on connects Workday Adaptive Planning to Google Sheets and Slides. Its purpose is to eliminate the need for manual comma-separated values CSV downloads.

title: OnePlus 16’s glowing rear lights look even cooler in action
summary: Borrowing a page from Nothing.
body: TL;DR New hands-on videos show the OnePlus 16’s “Interstellar Lighting Effect” in action across three rear illumination zones. The lights appear to use a fixed orange-yellow color and can blink or stay illuminated depending on the alert. The feature seems exclusive to the Tomorrow’s Starlight colorway, and the OnePlus 16 is not expected to launch officially in North America. It’s been just a few hours since we got our first proper official look at the OnePlus 16 , and we’re already getting a much better idea of what its most unique design upgrade looks like in action. Following Google’s HiLight feature and Nothing’s more established Glyph Matrix design , OnePlus is now putting its own spin on notification lighting on the rear of its latest device. The design, which the company is calling its “Interstellar Lighting Effect,” will reportedly notify users about incoming calls, texts, game highlights, and more. Up until the announcement, though, we’d only read about how the feature would work. Now, with hands-on videos out , we can finally see what OnePlus’ implementation looks like .

title: Google Nest Doorbells suffer mild identity crisis, start speaking with new accents
summary: Nest Doorbell glitch is causing automated voices to switch accents.
body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR Users in countries outside the US report that their Nest Doorbell announcements have inexplicably switched to an American accent. The issue reportedly does not occur with any other Google device interactions. One user claims that you can fix the issue by setting English (US) as your secondary language and deleting it after a few seconds. Google Home has had a flare-up of issues in recent days. Most recently, Voice Match has been struggling to identify who’s speaking. As Google toils away on a fix for that problem, another odd bug has shown up unannounced. This issue specifically affects the Nest Doorbell. Gemini for Home supports up to 10 languages, including English, French, German, Spanish, and Japanese. You can even pick a preferred accent, like US or UK English. While there may be some people who prefer to hear accents other than their own, most people tend to pick a voice that uses the same accent they do. Wouldn’t it be a bit jarring if your assistant suddenly started talking in your language but with a different accent?

title: Galaxy phones have an app delay problem, but Samsung is on the case
summary: Samsung is looking into app delays in hidden folders.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung is investigating an issue with DIY Home. Normal folders work as expected, but hidden folders are experiencing an app icon delay. Users report that the bug appeared after updating to One UI 9. Customization is one of the many reasons why Samsung fans love Galaxy phones. The Good Lock software suite opens up all kinds of possibilities to personalize your Android experience. However, just like any other software, Good Lock’s modules are not immune to bugs. And it appears the Home Up module is acting up after a recent update. Galaxy owners have identified an issue with DIY Home , a Home Up feature that allows you to freely arrange, rotate, resize, and overlap app icons, widgets, and folders. The issue in question concerns how icons appear in a hidden folder. As one user demonstrates in a screen recording, there’s a brief delay between when the hidden folder is opened and when the icons become visible. In contrast, there’s zero delay when opening a normal folder.

title: I spent two hours with Googlebooks. Here are the 8 most important things to know
summary: Googlebooks have arrived, and there's quite a lot to like.
body: It’s not every day we see a brand-new kind of laptop launch, let alone one with a new OS from a brand that’s never thought of as a rival to MacBooks or premium Windows machines. But Google’s giving it a shot anyway with its Googlebook family. This is both a new line of products and a fresh operating system, or, as Google would prefer you think of it, an “intelligence system,” in one. And the goals are noble ones — to offer a premium laptop that works with the devices of billions of Android users worldwide and delivers AI features in ways other PCs have yet to offer. I got to spend a couple of hours trying out the five different Googlebook models that Google is starting out with. These all offer the same software features, which we’ll look at first, but later we’ll check out the different form factors you’ll be able to buy come the start of October. There’s a lot to go over, but rest assured that everything Google and its partners have to show off adds up to some exciting productivity-focused machines with plenty of smarts and a number of fun touches.

title: The Pixel 11’s impressive voice typing feature is coming to Googlebooks
summary: Your laptop is finally ready to make sense of your rambling.
body: TL;DR Rambler, the smart voice-typing feature introduced with the Pixel 11, is coming to every Googlebook. Rambler can clean up messy dictation, remove mistakes, and organize spoken thoughts into useful notes and action items. Googlebooks also bring deeper Gemini integration, custom widgets, and developer tools, with prices starting at $899. We’ve been hearing about Google entering a new chapter in the laptop market for a while, and now it’s finally official. The company has fully launched Googlebook, its new Android-powered laptop platform that brings together Android, ChromeOS, Gemini, and hardware from several laptop makers. We’ve already covered the Googlebook announcement , the laptops announced today , and when you can actually buy one . But what caught my attention is just how much of the Android experience Google is bringing to these laptops. That includes Rambler, one of the more interesting features Google introduced with the Pixel 11 earlier this year, and it’s now coming to every Googlebook.

title: More Android phones in US, EU could finally get huge batteries, thanks to Apple
summary: Apple just showed Android OEMs how to get around battery capacity regulations.
body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Apple has revealed the Prepare to Ship feature for the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and we hope Android OEMs copy this option. This feature caps the iPhone’s battery capacity during transport, allowing the iPhone 18 Pro Max to meet transport requirements in many countries. The cap is removed once the phone is activated, allowing for higher battery capacities in Europe, the US, and other markets. Smartphone batteries have grown exponentially in the last few years, with 6,000mAh, 7,000mAh, and even 10,000mAh batteries on the market. Unfortunately, transport regulations in many markets place a cap on the size of an individual battery cell. This forces smartphone makers to adopt dual-cell battery designs or use smaller batteries, but Apple has revealed a nifty solution with the iPhone 18 Pro Max. Europe, the US, and international transport networks have a 20Wh cap on a small single-cell battery . That’s roughly equivalent to a maximum capacity of 5,300mAh. However, the iPhone 18 Pro Max has a 5,391mAh battery in global models. So how did Apple get around this restriction?

title: I’ve tested dozens of wireless chargers — this is the first one I actually want to keep using
summary: The first modular charging system I've used that actually works.
body: I’ve tested dozens of wireless chargers and desk setups over the years, and most of them suffer from the same problem. They all try to shoehorn everything into a single hub. There’s little, if any, flexibility in placement, choice of charging options, or future upgradeability. Moreover, as a design enthusiast, I care a lot about how a particular piece of tech looks in my space, and most chargers just aren’t very pretty to look at. But looks are subjective. Anyway, the fact is that most charging stations expect you to conform to a fixed layout for your phone, earbuds, and smartwatch . That’s fine for a functional product, but for one, the fixed layout has never really suited how I use my phone. Want to rearrange things? Tough luck.

title: This simple Duolingo trick brings back hearts and gets rid of the annoying ads
summary: If you hate what the app has become, you might want to give this a try.
body: Credit: Matt Horne / Android Authority Even as one of the last remaining Duolingo holdouts on the team, I can see how much worse Duolingo has become in recent years. The once-motivating gamification certainly appears to have been kicked up a few notches, and it’s the free users who’ve had it much worse. On the free plan, you’re bombarded with adverts for Super Duolingo and third-party games that you can’t skip for several seconds. Even worse, the heart system that allowed you to keep practicing until you made five mistakes was replaced by an energy bar that runs down even if you’re nailing the answers. That’s why I was excited to learn about a very simple trick that returns you to a simpler version of Duolingo — one with the hearts system, no ads at all, fewer clicks between lessons, and less gamification.

title: The iPhone 18 Pro isn’t worth $1,200, and the Pixel 11 Pro proves it
summary: Google's offering just feels more at home for some reason.
body: While the new iPhone Duo has received a lot of fanfare, the standard iPhone 18 Pro is going to be the one driving most of Apple’s sales. It doesn’t look much different from the iPhone 17 Pro on the outside, but Apple’s presentation was full of internal changes, from better battery performance to a new physically adjustable camera aperture. All those features do seem tempting at first glance, but I’d still go with the Pixel 11 Pro any day — just because it’s a much better overall purchase than its Apple counterpart.

title: I use Google Maps every day, but Apple Maps still does these 4 things better
summary: Google Maps is great, but Apple Maps gets these four things surprisingly right.
body: Be it a daily morning commute or a long road trip, most of us spend a surprising amount of time looking at Google Maps even without realizing it. Beyond the usual in-car navigation, it is my go-to when I’m looking for a new coffee shop or just checking transit schedules in a new country. And yet, lately, I find myself popping open Apple Maps more often than I expected. Apple has spent the last decade rebuilding Maps into a surprisingly capable navigation app. It might not beat Google Maps just yet, as Google still has the edge when it comes to local search and the sheer amount of information available. However, Apple has a few areas where its approach is simply better. Here are the things I prefer about Apple Maps and want Google Maps to copy.

title: I tested the Pixel 11 Pro XL’s 25W wireless charging — and it’s still way too slow
summary: PixelSnap is faster on the Pixel 11 Pro XL, but charging is still slow and hot.
body: Pixels and I get on reasonably well, but if there’s one area that I find myself constantly sighing loudly at, it’s charging the darn phones. Yes, you can just splash the cash on official accessories like the Pixel Flex 67W charger (), a mighty impressive USB-C adapter in its own right. But not all the accessories in Google’s charging ecosystem are as good — and I’m pointing fingers squarely at the PixelSnap charger (). I’m still disappointed that Google has essentially abandoned my beloved Pixel Stand in favor of PixelSnap. While MagSafe undoubtedly has some conveniences for case accessories, it’s proven to be a significant downgrade in terms of what actually matters — charging times. Last year’s Pixel 10 Pro XL using PixelSnap proved to be over half an hour slower than the Pixel 9 Pro XL on the old Pixel Stand.

title: 5 smartwatches you should buy instead of the Moto Watch Ultra
summary: There are a lot of great options out there.
body: The Moto Watch Ultra is Motorola’s latest smartwatch, featuring a unique blend of features for the price. The singular variant costs $350 and includes LTE eSIM support, Wear OS 6, a 1.5-inch pOLED display, and Polar’s health and fitness tracking algorithms. That’s a fabulous combination in itself, but Motorola has cut corners on the processor and is only offering two OS upgrades. Thankfully, there’s no shortage of good Wear OS smartwatch options in the market. From Google to Samsung, there are plenty of great alternatives you should consider first. So, before settling on the Moto Watch Ultra, consider these five other alternatives.

title: I used Immich for years, but this self-hosted Google Photos alternative is even better
summary: Noodle Gallery takes everything I love about Immich and adds smarter ways to share, organize, and manage family photos.
body: I’ve had Immich running on my home server for the past three years. It’s a self-hosting essential for me as I try to offload as much of my backups and services from the cloud as possible. It’s where I keep the photos from my SLR, where my phone backs up photos automatically, and where I can search through years of images without handing everything over to Google. For a self-hosted alternative to Google Photos , there’s little doubt that Immich is the go-to for most. But as good as Immich is, as an enthusiast, I was bound to run into limitations. Immich is great at managing individual photo libraries, but it isn’t always great at managing a family’s photo library. If you’re trying to share a portion of your library, Immich makes it extremely hard. And you can absolutely forget about sharing certain aspects of the library, like metadata.

title: Gemini’s rough patch with smart home controls has spread to Android Auto
summary: One Gemini smart home bug gets fixed, another pops up.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Some Android Auto users say Gemini has suddenly stopped controlling their smart home devices. The issue follows recent Gemini smart home control problems on Wear OS, which Google said it had fixed. It’s not clear what’s causing the Android Auto problem — we’ve reached out to Google for comment. Gemini has had a rough couple of weeks with smart home controls. Wear OS users recently reported that Gemini would claim it had controlled lights, AC units, and other devices when nothing actually happened , before Google said that the issue had been fixed . It isn’t clear if it’s related, but some Android Auto users are now finding that Gemini suddenly refuses to control their smart home devices, even though those same commands worked previously. In a post on the r/AndroidAuto subreddit earlier today, one user says that Gemini has stopped executing commands such as turning on the AC. Instead, it now responds that it “cannot control smart home devices through Google Maps while driving.” The poster says the feature had been working for months before this change.

title: Android 17 QPR1 fixes a major headache for enthusiasts
summary: No more turning developer options off to check your bank account.
body: TL;DR Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Pixel phones now. The update no longer allows third-party apps to see whether you have developer settings or USB debugging active. This should make life easier for anyone who tinkers with Android’s more advanced settings. Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out now to Pixel phones going back to the Pixel 6. The update brings a number of changes, including UI tweaks, the option to include photo location metadata in images shared through Android’s media picker, and more. As spotted by a user on X, QPR1 also quietly fixes an issue that’s been a thorn in the side of Android enthusiasts for years. As developer Sameera Wijerahna points out in a post on X , Android 17 QPR1 no longer lets third-party apps see the state of developer options or debugging settings. This could be a big deal for developers or anyone else who likes to tinker with their Android devices — prior to the change, some apps wouldn’t open on devices with certain settings active.

summary: Quicker VIP switching and a refreshed layout are now landing on Pixels.
body: TL;DR Google is rolling out the Pixel VIPs redesign announced with the September Pixel Drop. The update adds faster VIP switching, reorganizes local updates, and refreshes the interface with Material 3 Expressive styling. Google has also removed the old “Things to do together” recommendations section. Google came into the September Pixel Drop with a list of upgrades for Pixel VIPs , but there was one catch: It didn’t actually show us what most of them looked like. We did manage to get an early look at the redesigned home screen widget , but the rest of the experience was still largely hidden. That’s changing now with Pixel VIPs version 2.0.97, which is starting to roll out, and we’ve captured a full gallery and video showing the refreshed VIP page in action. The biggest change becomes obvious as soon as you open a VIP from the widget. A new floating navigation strip sits at the bottom, letting you swipe between VIPs without backing out to the widget first. You can also jump straight to someone by tapping their profile picture in the strip. Long-press the bar and left and right arrows appear, giving you another way to move through the list.

title: Android Auto may finally be fixing this annoying dashboard bug
summary: The fix is showing up in Android Auto v17.8 beta.
body: TL;DR Android Auto’s missing cellular signal bars are starting to return for some users. The fix appears in Android Auto version 17.8.1638, which is currently a beta build. Availability is still inconsistent, so stable users may have to wait a little longer. When you’re driving through a patchy coverage area, those tiny signal bars on the Android Auto dashboard can be surprisingly useful. A quick glance at the dashboard tells you whether your connection is holding up before a call starts breaking up. But for some Android Auto users, that glance has been useless for months because the cellular signal indicator simply disappeared. Now, Android Auto version 17.8.1638 appears to be bringing it back. The issue surfaced earlier this year, with users reporting that Android Auto had stopped showing their phone’s cellular signal strength . As we noted at the time, the bug was mostly cosmetic, as calls, mobile data, and navigation continued working normally. That didn’t make it any less annoying for drivers who rely on the indicator to know when they’re heading into a dead zone.

title: This Good Lock module turns Samsung’s Gallery app into a more capable editor
summary: It's quite good, but Samsung should make it even better.
body: Samsung’s Gallery app is more than just an image and video viewer. It lets you edit images and videos, turn images into collages and GIFs, and remove backgrounds and undesired objects from images. You can also enable Gallery Labs — a secret menu in Gallery — to unlock additional functionality like album-entry locks and the ability to save images as a PDF. But that’s not all. Samsung offers a Good Lock module that extends Gallery’s functionality even further. It’s called Gallery Assistant, and it can be really handy if you need to carry out batch image and video operations/manipulations on your Galaxy phone.

title: I used Spectrum Mobile for 4 months. Here’s why I went right back to Visible
summary: Well, that didn't last long.
body: I’ve switched phone carriers more in the last 18 months than I have in my entire adult life. After a decade as T-Mobile customers, my partner and I switched to Visible last year and had a really fantastic experience. Our service was great, the plan features were just what we needed, and the price was extremely fair. But about a year after using Visible, we got an offer from Spectrum Mobile we couldn’t refuse . The offer? Two lines of Spectrum Mobile Unlimited Plus and 1Gbps home internet service for just $100/month total ($30/month for each phone line, plus $40/month for our internet). It was a seriously good deal, and despite hearing horror stories about Spectrum Mobile, I went against my better judgment and signed up anyway.
